No more hand-written code? Epic's Disney project reportedly shifts to 'AI-First' development
Developers working on the upcoming Star Wars and Marvel shooter have been reportedly instructed to lean heavily on AI, especially during the creation of code and art.
Alissa McAloon
,
Editorial Director
,
GameDeveloper.com
October 14, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Epic Games has reportedly mandated a sizable shift to its development principles, with Bloomberg reporting that the company has delayed an upcoming Disney game amid the project’s shift to an “AI-first” production model.
The change, which was backed up in part by a social media statement from Epic CEO Tim Sweeney shortly after publication, marks a very high-profile adoption of generative AI tools in a field where use of the nascent tech is still considered controversial among some developers and players.
According to
the Bloomberg report
, developers working on the upcoming Star Wars and Marvel shooter have been instructed to lean heavily on AI during development, especially during the creation of code and art. In an email reviewed by the publication, the game’s director reportedly told developers that the title’s art should be “generated with full AI workflows” and to use “no more hand-written code”. News of the pivot was paired with a delay: the game’s release is shifting away from its March target and to a new but yet-unrevealed release date further down the line.
Related:
Unity unveils Unity Spark, an prompt-based tool for Google's AI game platform
Shortly after rumors of the AI pivot started to circulate in the wake of Bloomberg’s recording,
Sweeney took to X
to share a statement on Epic Games’ approach toward AI and how that approach is in the middle of a major change.
“We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration,” reads Sweeney’s X post. “The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”
It’s worth calling out here that Sweeney commented on Epic’s AI approach at large and did not comment on or confirm the specific claims surrounding the Disney project from Bloomberg’s report.
